pages.hook: In the USA, people talk about the weather all the time. It is the easiest way to start a friendly chat with a neighbor, a driver or a stranger in line.
pages.polite: Start with **Nice day, isn’t it?** or **Cold enough for you?** Then ask a short question to keep talking.

mythfact.s: In the USA, the weather is a common small-talk topic.
mythfact.why: Saying “Nice day, huh?” is a normal way to start a conversation.

mythfact.s: Americans usually say the temperature in Celsius.
mythfact.why: The USA mostly uses Fahrenheit, not Celsius.

mythfact.s: Water freezes at 32 degrees Fahrenheit.
mythfact.why: 32°F is the same as 0°C.

mythfact.s: The weather is the same in every part of the USA.
mythfact.why: The USA is very big: Florida is warm and Alaska is very cold.

mythfact.s: Chicago has the nickname “the Windy City”.
mythfact.why: Chicago is famous by this nickname. It is often linked to the wind off Lake Michigan, but some people say it was about talkative politicians.

lines: Bring a warm coat and a hat.
See you at the park at 3!

opts: A warm coat and a hat
decode.why: “Bring a warm coat and a hat.”

compare.br: In Brazil, people say “Que calor!” or “Tá chovendo” and use Celsius: 30 degrees is a hot day.
compare.us: In the USA, people use Fahrenheit: 85 degrees is hot and 30 degrees is very cold. Chicago has hot summers and snowy winters.
compare.tip: Do not worry about the numbers. Say hot, warm, cool or cold.
compare.ask: What is the weather like today where you live? Say it in English.

quiz.q: A neighbor says, “Nice morning, isn’t it?” You say…
quiz.why: Agree and add a short comment.
In English the weather needs It’s.

quiz.q: Which temperature scale is common in the USA?
quiz.why: Fahrenheit is the everyday scale in the USA.

pages.title: Reading quest — Four seasons, one city · part 1
text: Hello from **Chicago**! I live here, and the weather is always a topic. People say, “**Nice day, huh?**” in the elevator, at the bus stop and in the café.
In **summer**, it is very hot and sunny. We go to the lake and eat ice cream. In **autumn**, it is cool and windy. The trees are red and yellow. Chicago has a nickname: the Windy City.

In **winter**, it is freezing! There is a lot of snow, and I say, “**Brr! Bundle up.**” I wear a warm coat, a hat and gloves. When it is pouring rain, I bring an umbrella. **It’s freezing out there!**

scan.ans: a warm coat, a hat and gloves

pages.title: Reading quest — Four seasons, one city · part 2
text: In **spring**, the days are warm again. Flowers come out, and the birds sing. Last week, I listened to “The Four Seasons” by Antonio Vivaldi. It is a famous piece of music from Italy, from about 1725. It has one part for each season. In the spring part, you can hear birds.
Which season do you like? I like spring, but my friend Evan likes snow. He says, “**I need a warm coat**,” and then he laughs. Write soon, and **stay warm**!

speed.q: Complete a fala: “____ out there!” (Está um gelo lá fora!)
Complete a fala: “____ rain!” (Está chovendo a cântaros!)

opts: Eu gostaria de sorvete de baunilha.
Certo. Vou levar quatro, por favor.
Nossa. Preciso de um casaco quente.

errors.wrong: Is cold today.
errors.fix: It’s cold today.
errors.why: English needs the subject It for weather.

errors.wrong: I am cold in Chicago in winter.
errors.fix: It is cold in Chicago in winter.
errors.why: I am cold = my body feels cold. It is cold = the weather.

errors.wrong: It’s raining a lot of.
errors.fix: It’s raining a lot.
errors.why: A lot ends the sentence by itself.

errors.wrong: In the summer is very hot.
errors.fix: It is very hot in summer.
errors.why: Start with It is, and use in summer without the.

pages.title: Boss mission — What's the weather?

brief.teacher: You are Evan. Change the plan during the scene.
brief.student: You meet your neighbor Evan on a cold morning in Chicago. Talk about the weather. You are the customer / visitor.

complications: The other person did not hear you: repeat.

pages.title: Free production
pages.prompt: Você conta o que faz no ano. Diga o que acontece ou o que você faz em duas estações, com in. Ligue à referência Four Seasons: é o concerto das quatro estações do ano.
pages.model: I swim in summer. It snows in winter. Flowers grow in spring. Four Seasons helps here.

items: Write 5 sentences about the weather in your city.
Record yourself saying “Nice day, huh?” and 2 answers.
Review: It’s sunny / cold / windy / hot. Stay warm!

pages.title: Mission complete
recap: Yes, very hot. And in winter, snow!
